newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Clarke says he not afraid raise rates.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Clarke says he not afraid raise rates.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Sunday he was not afraid to raise interest rates if inflationary pressures built up.

"The markets believe, apparently, that I won't put up interest rates in any circumstances this side of an election. That is nonsense," he told GMTV from the Washington meeting of G7 finance ministers. "The judgement I will make is if I think this low inflation, below 2.5 percent, is not going to be maintained unless I cut interest rates, then I will move interest rates," he said.

He warned right-wingers in his ruling Conservative party who are pressing for tax cuts in his November budget that such reductions would not necessarily secure victory in the next election, due within the next eight months.
"Frothy tax cuts won't win a vote. It is not the case that my budget requires tax cuts in order to win the election," the Chancellor of the Exchequer said.

"The public will be deeply suspicious of any tax cuts because they remember we promised tax cuts last time and unfortunately weren't able to deliver them, so they will look sideways at tax cuts from this government.
"I completely reject the idea that the next election is entirely determined by whether or not I can lop "X' amount off tax in November."
